name: Question 15
problem: The velocity $v,$ in meters per second, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨-\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2,\,t⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1\,\text{s},$ rounded to one decimal place.
worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}.
$$

First, we evaluate $v(1):$

$$
v(1)=⟨0,\,2,\,1⟩
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and evaluating it at $t=1,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{t},\,0,\,1⟩, \\ a(1) & =⟨-1,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(1)\times a(1),||v(1)||,$ and $||v(1)\times a(1)||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1)\times a(1) & =⟨0,\,2,\,1⟩\times ⟨-1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨2,-1,2⟩, \\ ||v(1)|| & =\sqrt{0)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5}, \\ ||v(1)\times a(1)|| & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration at $t=1,$ and we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v(1)\times a(1)||}{||v(1)||} \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & ≈1.3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the normal component of acceleration is approximately 
 $1.3\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$

Question 15
?

The velocity v, in meters per second, of a particle P at time t is given by v(t)=⟨−ln⁡t,2,t⟩. Find the normal component of the acceleration of P at time t=1s, rounded to one decimal place.

a
1.5ms−2
b
0.6ms−2
c
1.7ms−2
d
 1.3ms−2
e
0.8ms−2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The normal component of acceleration is given by aN=||v×a||||v||.

First, we evaluate v(1): v(1)=⟨0,2,1⟩

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and evaluating it at t=1, as follows: a=⟨ddt(−ln⁡t),ddt(2),ddt(t)⟩=⟨−1t,0,1⟩,a(1)=⟨−1,0,1⟩

Then, we compute v(1)×a(1),||v(1)||, and ||v(1)×a(1)||: v(1)×a(1)=⟨0,2,1⟩×⟨−1,0,1⟩=ijk021−101=2101i−01−11j+02−10k=⟨2,−1,2⟩,||v(1)||=0)2+22+12=5,||v(1)×a(1)||=22+(−1)2+22=9=3

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration at t=1, and we get aN=||v(1)×a(1)||||v(1)||=35≈1.3.

Therefore, the normal component of acceleration is approximately 1.3ms−2.
